facts.statement: The species was originally known as Buchanosteus murrumbidgeensis before being moved to a new genus.
The genus Parabuchanosteus was established in 1972 after a re-examination of the species originally described in 1952.
facts.quote: It was originally described as Buchanosteus murrumbidgeensis in 1952. In 1972, it was re-examined and promoted to a new genus.

facts.statement: Parabuchanosteus belongs to the family Parabuchanosteidae.
This animal is classified as a placoderm.
Fossils of Parabuchanosteus have been found in Late Emsian marine rocks in New South Wales, Australia.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Late Emsian-aged marine strata of the Murrumbidgee Group in New South Wales, Australia.

facts.statement: Parabuchanosteus lived between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: The species was first described by White in 1952.
facts.quote: It was originally described as Buchanosteus murrumbidgeensis in 1952.
